verdict.rationale: Honeycomb documents an official MCP server that any MCP-capable external agent can connect to in order to query live telemetry, fetch traces and investigate latency or error spikes. It also offers a documented REST API with a downloadable OpenAPI spec, and a community user reports using Honeycomb's MCP server as an agent tool during incidents. The probe's 404s were on different paths than the documented /api/openapi-public.yaml, so they do not contradict the spec claim. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that metrics and logs (as distinct from traces) are each queryable through the agent tools, and more detailed independent hands-on evidence of production debugging.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an external agent query metrics, logs, and traces through documented APIs to debug production

citations.quote: Connect Honeycomb to any AI agent that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) so it can query your telemetry, investigate issues, and answer questions using your live Honeycomb data.
Each tool corresponds to a specific Honeycomb capability, like running a query, fetching a trace, or creating a Board.
Investigate and diagnose latency or error spikes
You can [download the Honeycomb OpenAPI spec](/api/openapi-public.yaml) to use with your own tooling.
In Honeycomb, traces and logs are stored as _structured events_: labeled JSON objects sent over HTTP, indexed automatically on every field at ingest, and queryable without a predefined schema.
